protected_group: The nonexclusive 18-category definition includes state constitutional officers, legislators, active or retired state and specified federal or tribal judges, court commissioners, State Bar Court judges, prosecutors, public defenders, local elected officials, specified appointees, police chiefs, sheriffs, public safety officials, administrative law judges, and court-appointed children's counsel in family or dependency proceedings. Each separate voter or DMV statute has its own eligibility list.
effective_date: The clean AB 343 definition is effectiveJanuary 1, 2026. The current agency Internet rule reflects AB 1785, effectiveJanuary 1, 2025. Civil Code 1798.84.1 added by AB 1521 is effectiveJanuary 1, 2026.
sunset_date: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.
property_records_online: Section 7928.205 prohibits an agency from publicly posting the home address, telephone number, or both name and assessor parcel number associated with the home address, without written permission. A legally required notice or publication remains allowed.
voter_records: Section 2166.7 provides a separate public-safety-officer application route only if the county board authorizes it. The applicant declares a life-threatening circumstance under penalty of perjury. The application is public. Its officer definition is limited to specified subdivisions of Government Code 7920.535.
drivers_license_records: Vehicle Code 1808.4 protects home addresses in DMV records on request for its separately enumerated persons. Courts, law enforcement, BOE, specified subpoena-based attorney access, and legally entitled agencies remain exceptions. Records may remain open with the address removed.
public_records_requests: The cited rule addresses unrestricted agency Internet posting. Separate general public-records request exemptions are not established by this section alone.
publication_takedown: AB 1521 repealed former Government Code 7928.210 through 7928.230. The former written-demand takedown provisions must not be presented as current. Current Civil Code 1798.84.1 instead addresses Internet solicitation, sale or trade of covered contact information with intent to cause imminent great bodily harm. It is not an ordinary written-notice deletion rule.
route: For the agency Internet rule, the official's written permission is needed before the agency posts covered information. Voter and DMV requests use separate statutory procedures.
duration: Channel-specific. Voter confidentiality under 2166.7 lasts no more than two years and may be renewed for another period no longer than two years. Section 1808.4 provides permanent address suppression on request for specified retired judges or peace officers, with separate survivor periods and exceptions. No single duration applies to all channels.
limits: The agency Internet rule retains legally required notices. The voter application is public and has its own risk and county-authorization conditions. The DMV provision has its own categories and disclosure exceptions. The 18-category agency definition does not automatically determine voter or DMV eligibility.
litigation_status: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.

protected_group: Thirteen employment categories under subsection (a), plus the separate municipal election-worker rule in subsection (d).
effective_date: 2024-07-01 for the election-worker amendment under P.A.24-148 section 31.
sunset_date: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.
property_records_online: Subsection (e) preserves documents defined in 7-35 bb and lists under 12-55. This section cannot support blanket land-record or tax-roll suppression.
voter_records: The section preserves unredacted disclosure of lists prepared under title 9. Separate voter provisions were not researched.
drivers_license_records: This section expressly does not apply to DMV records described in section 14-10. That is a scope exclusion, not a finding that no other protection exists.
public_records_requests: Employer personnel, medical and similar files receive the subsection (a) rule. Non-employer requests require a written confidentiality request and business address. Subsection (c) distinguishes named-person requests and electronic lists from other records.
publication_takedown: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.
route: Submit the subsection (c) written request and business address to the holding agency. Municipal election personnel use the separate municipality request in subsection (d).
duration: The separate municipal election-worker rule runs from 90 days before an election or a later request to 90 days after the election, subject to its office exception.
limits: Complaints go to the FOI Commission. The section requires a willful and knowing violation for its penalty and creates no private right of action.
litigation_status: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.

category_catalog: [{"paragraph": "section-specific definition", "statutory_text": "(1) A person shall not knowingly make available on the world wide web the personal information of a peace officer, corrections person, justice, judge, commissioner, public defender, or prosecutor if the dissemination of the personal information poses an imminent and serious threat to the peace officer's, corrections person's, justice's, judge's, commissioner's, public defender's, or prosecutor's safety or the safety of that person's immediate family and the threat is reasonably apparent to the person making the information available on the world wide web to be serious and imminent. (2) It is not a violation of this section if an employee of a county auditor or county assessor publishes personal information, in good faith, on the website of the county auditor or county assessor in the ordinary course of carrying out public functions. (3) For the purposes of this section: (a) \"Commissioner\" means a commissioner of the superior court, court of appeals, or supreme court. (b) \"Corrections person\" means any employee or volunteer who by state, county, municipal, or combination thereof, statute has the responsibility for the confinement, care, management, training, treatment, education, supervision, or counseling of those whose civil rights have been limited in some way by legal sanction. (c) \"Immediate family\" means a peace officer's, corrections person's, justice's, judge's, commissioner's, public defender's, or prosecutor's spouse, child, or parent and any other adult who lives in the same residence as the person. (d) \"Judge\" means a judge of the United States district court, the United States court of appeals, the United States magistrate, the United States bankruptcy court, and the Washington court of appeals, superior court, district court, or municipal court. (e) \"Justice\" means a justice of the United States supreme court or Washington supreme court. (f) \"Personal information\" means a peace officer's, corrections person's, justice's, judge's, commissioner's, public defender's, or prosecutor's home address, home telephone number, pager number, social security number, home email address, directions to the person's home, or photographs of the person's home or vehicle. (g) \"Prosecutor\" means a county prosecuting attorney, a city attorney, the attorney general, or a United States attorney and their assistants or deputies. (h) \"Public defender\" means a federal public defender, or other public defender, and his or her assistants or deputies."}]

category_catalog: [{"paragraph": "section-specific definition", "statutory_text": "\"Covered public servant\" means: (1) The governor; (2) The lieutenant governor; (3) The administrative director appointed pursuant to section 26-3; (4) Any head of a department established under section 26-4; (5) Any member of the legislature; (6) Any active, formerly active, or retired: (A) Justice of the Hawaii supreme court; (B) Judge of the Hawaii intermediate appellate court; (C) Judge of a Hawaii circuit court or circuit family court; (D) Judge of a Hawaii district court or district family court; or (E) Per diem judge of a Hawaii district court or district family court; (7) Any active, formerly active, or retired: (A) Justice of the United States Supreme Court; (B) Judge of the United States Court of Appeals; (C) Judge or magistrate judge of the United States District Court; or (D) Judge of the United States Bankruptcy Court, who resides in the State, formerly resided in the State while serving as a federal judge, or owns real property in the State; (8) The administrative director of the courts; (9) The deputy administrative director of the courts; (10) Any employee or volunteer of the office of elections; or (11) Any person designated for good cause by the governor, president of the senate, speaker of the house of representatives, chief justice, chief judge of the United States District Court for the District of Hawaii, or chairperson of the office of Hawaiian affairs in the designator's respective body. \"Family\" means spouses or reciprocal beneficiaries, former spouses or former reciprocal beneficiaries, persons who have a child in common, parents, children, persons related by consanguinity, and persons jointly residing or formerly residing in the same dwelling unit."}]

protected_group: Specified federal judges and immediate family. The definitions and exceptions in sections 5933 and 5937 must accompany any summary.
effective_date: The default is enactment. Specified provisions in 5934(c)(1), (d) and (e) take effect 120 days after enactment. The excerpt retains the exact rule without replacing it with an unverified calendar calculation.
sunset_date: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.
property_records_online: Section 5934(c) establishes grants to states. It does not by itself establish a universal closure rule for every state property record.
voter_records: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.
drivers_license_records: The DPPA, 18 U.S.C.2721, restricts state-DMV disclosure of personal information and highly restricted information, subject to statutory exceptions and permissible uses. It is a separate general motor-vehicle-record law, not a judicial-privacy request to remove all public websites.
public_records_requests: Federal agencies receiving a proper request mark covered information private and remove it from availability within 72 hours, subject to the section's exceptions.
publication_takedown: Section 5934(d) separately regulates knowing data-broker transfers and private Internet publication after written request, including a 72-hour removal requirement.
route: The at-risk individual or agent submits statutory written notice. The Administrative Office or appropriate Article I court may act as the judge's agent.
duration: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.
limits: The act preserves specified news/public-concern speech, consent and government sharing. Section 5934(d) also contains publication/source exceptions and the data-broker definition has exclusions.
litigation_status: Not verified. No conclusion about protection or its absence.

category_catalog: [{"paragraph": "section-specific definition", "statutory_text": "(1) At-risk individual.--The term at-risk individual'' means-- (A) a Federal judge; (B) a senior, recalled, or retired Federal judge; (C) any individual who is the spouse, parent, sibling, or child of an individual described in subparagraph (A) or (B); (D) any individual to whom an individual described in subparagraph (A) or (B) stands in loco parentis; or [[Page 136 STAT. 3460]] (E) any other individual living in the household of an individual described in subparagraph (A) or (B)."}]
